entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD AI Principles), OECD/LEGAL/0449, 2019, revised 2024 - a recommendation, not binding law, Principle 1.4
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (as amended incl. No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025; adilet.zan.kz, English unofficial translation)
entries.provision: Art. 22 para 1 subparas 1-3 (measures to protect personal data and minimise adverse consequences). The fund is fictional and the data synthetic, so the law does not bind this prototype; it is used as the benchmark the fund would face if it operated in Kazakhstan, where it would be the owner/operator of applicants' personal data.
entries.why_here: Part 1 used only clean profiles, so validation is preventive: an impossible value (GPA 9.9) must never reach a model that shortlisted 356/400 applicants and would score it anyway.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD AI Principles), OECD/LEGAL/0449, 2019, revised 2024 - a recommendation, not binding law, Principle 1.2
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (as amended incl. No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025; adilet.zan.kz, English unofficial translation)
entries.provision: Art. 7 para 9 (personal data excessive in content and scope relative to the purpose shall not be processed). The fund is fictional and the data synthetic, so the law does not bind this prototype; it is used as the benchmark the fund would face if it operated in Kazakhstan, where it would be the owner/operator of applicants' personal data.
entries.why_here: Part 1 found flagship-university applicants scored +2.5 points higher than identical regional ones (95% CI +1.1 to +4.1, sign p = 0.002) and 4/40 gender-name flips; name and university are not merit, so the model no longer sees them.

entries.principle: Respect for human rights and privacy (lawful, purpose-bound processing)
entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD AI Principles), OECD/LEGAL/0449, 2019, revised 2024 - a recommendation, not binding law, Principle 1.2
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (as amended incl. No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025; adilet.zan.kz, English unofficial translation)
entries.provision: Art. 7 paras 1 and 8 (processing only with consent and only for specific, predetermined, legitimate goals) and Art. 8 para 1 (consent by the individual or their legal representative). The fund is fictional and the data synthetic, so the law does not bind this prototype; it is used as the benchmark the fund would face if it operated in Kazakhstan, where it would be the owner/operator of applicants' personal data.
entries.why_here: The bare pipeline screens anything it is given, including a minor, an applicant without consent, a request to rank by ethnicity and a name field carrying an instruction to the model; none of these may be processed.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD AI Principles), OECD/LEGAL/0449, 2019, revised 2024 - a recommendation, not binding law, Principle 1.5
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (as amended incl. No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025; adilet.zan.kz, English unofficial translation)
entries.provision: Art. 22 para 1 subpara 5 (registration and recording of actions) and Art. 12 para 2 (storage within the Republic of Kazakhstan). The fund is fictional and the data synthetic, so the law does not bind this prototype; it is used as the benchmark the fund would face if it operated in Kazakhstan, where it would be the owner/operator of applicants' personal data.
entries.why_here: The divergences in Part 1 were only visible because every decision was counted; one record per call, refusals and escalations included, lets an auditor check a decision later without re-running the model, while storing field names and a hash rather than applicants' values.

entries.principle: Human oversight (human agency and the ability to contest a decision)
entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD AI Principles), OECD/LEGAL/0449, 2019, revised 2024 - a recommendation, not binding law, Principle 1.2
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 'On Personal Data and their Protection' (as amended incl. No. 231-VIII of 17.11.2025; adilet.zan.kz, English unofficial translation)
entries.provision: Art. 19-1 paras 1-3 (automated processing that changes or terminates a subject's rights is prohibited without consent; the subject must be able to object, and the objection must be considered within three working days). The fund is fictional and the data synthetic, so the law does not bind this prototype; it is used as the benchmark the fund would face if it operated in Kazakhstan, where it would be the owner/operator of applicants' personal data.
entries.why_here: Part 1 showed rejects (20-45) and shortlists (45-85) overlap only in 40-49, so scores there are uncertain; those, low-income rejects and contradictory replies go to a person rather than being decided by the machine alone.
